newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end off highs after BHP slips.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end off highs after BHP slips.

text.p: The Australian share market closed slightly firmer on Tuesday but early gains were pared by the performance of bellwether BHP which dipped on comments by its managing director and profit downgrades by major brokers.
The key All Ordinaries index closed 5.1 points higher at 2,255.9, well off its intraday high of 2267.5.
The September share price index futures contracted finished 11 points up at 2,264 and at a 8.1 point premium to the underlying index.
BHP managing director John Prescott told Reuters the steel market may be worsening and that the copper price remained a challenge for the world's second largest copper producer.

The market's performance was disappointing following Wall Street's surge on Monday, said dealer Diane Jenner of Sydney brokerage Dicksons. Jenner said Prescott's mid-morning comments about the domestic steel market and the international copper market helped drive the company's shares lower.
Prescott's negative comments followed a number of recent profit downgrades for BHP by Australian analysts.
Dealers said the outlook for Australian shares on Wednesday remained dependent on volatile U.S. markets but they said a Dow pullback after its two-day surge would not be overly negative.

Companies reporting on Tuesday included GIO Insurance which posted a flat full year net profit of A$142 million ($114 million). Its shares were slightly firmer early but weakened as the overall market eased from its highs.
Gaming machine manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure reported its maiden result as a listed company, posting a full year net profit of A$17.84 million.
Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids said its year net profit rose to A$51.8 million from A$46.3 million.
Rises narrowly outnumbered falls on the day while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
